html:
Using your kitchen speaker

To start a timer, say “Hey assistant, set a timer for ten minutes.” To add milk to your list, say “Hey assistant, add milk to my shopping list.” The speaker answers out loud.

category: article quoting an attack phrase (override boundary)
html:
Why chatbots fall for “ignore previous instructions”

Researchers found that some chatbots obey text such as “ignore previous instructions” when it appears inside a web page they summarise. The article explains how developers keep page text separate from the instructions they give their own software.

category: docs with a tool-call example (fake_message boundary)
html:
How tool calls look

When the model wants to use a tool, the API returns a message like this example:

{"role": "assistant", "tool_call": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Lisbon"}}}

Your code runs the tool and sends the result back.

category: chat API docs with role names (fake_message boundary)
html:
Message roles

Each message has a role: system for your app's own instructions, user for what the person typed, and assistant for the model's replies. Example: [{"role": "system", "content": "You answer questions about trains."}]

html:
Spotting fake bank emails

Scam emails often say your account will close unless you reply with a one-time code. A real bank never asks for one. Delete the message and contact your bank directly.

html:
Writing alt text

Screen readers read alt text aloud to people who can't see the image. Describe what matters in the picture in one short sentence, and leave out “image of”.
